extraction.name: C-EVAL
extraction.description: A comprehensive Chinese evaluation suite for foundation models. It contains multiple-choice questions across four difficulty levels and 52 disciplines, and includes a harder subset called C-EVAL HARD.
extraction.creator: Yuzhen Huang, Yuzhuo Bai, Zhihao Zhu, Junlei Zhang, Jinghan Zhang, Tangjun Su, Junteng Liu, Chuancheng Lv, Yikai Zhang, Jiayi Lei, Yao Fu, Maosong Sun, Junxian He
extraction.publisher: NeurIPS 2023 Track on Datasets and Benchmarks
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The primary source of the data is mock exams freely available on the internet. In addition, some college-level questions are past exam questions from top universities in China, publicly shared by students, and a minor fraction are mock questions for the national graduate entrance exam sourced from the Weipu website. The collected materials were parsed from PDF/Microsoft Word documents and some web pages, then automatically or manually structured, deduplicated, cleaned, and human-validated by the authors.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Questions with fewer than four options were eliminated, and for questions with more than four options, incorrect choices were randomly dropped.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Multiple-choice exam questions from mock exams, past university exam questions, and mock national graduate entrance exam questions; the source materials were mainly PDF or Microsoft Word documents, with a minor fraction as web pages.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Questions were parsed into a structured format automatically when possible and otherwise manually by the authors; complex mathematical notations were manually converted into standard LATEX; all questions underwent several rounds of human validation by the authors; for explanation data, GPT-4 first generated step-by-step explanations and these were then human annotated/revised to produce high-quality explanation data.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Human validation was performed in several rounds, and LATEX notations were checked to ensure they compiled without syntax errors.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-4 was used to generate step-by-step explanations for the development split.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The benchmark is described as challenging and intended for a Chinese context, but the authors note it is still incomplete and that broader evaluation should consider other aspects such as safety, bias, and robustness.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark is far from perfect for LLM evaluation and does not cover many abilities beyond accuracy, such as reasoning over APIs and other non-accuracy aspects.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper frames the benchmark as helping developers prepare LLMs for more complex scenarios and making progress on evaluation in a Chinese context.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Evaluation of LLMs, specifically as a challenging evaluation suite/benchmark; the text implies use for testing model capabilities rather than training.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The development split exemplars were annotated with explanations for few-shot chain-of-thought settings, and GPT-4 was prompted to generate step-by-step explanations for the development split.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: PDF documents were processed into text; questions were parsed into a structured format; complex mathematical notations were manually converted into standard LaTeX; questions were filtered to exactly four choices by eliminating those with fewer than four options and randomly dropping incorrect choices for questions with more than four options; deduplication and cleaning were applied; human validation ensured LaTeX syntax correctness; typos and incorrect formats from PDF documents were fixed.

name.evidence: We present C-EVAL, the first comprehensive Chinese evaluation suite designed to assess advanced knowledge and reasoning abilities of foundation models in a Chinese context.

description.evidence: C-EVAL comprises multiple-choice questions across four difficulty levels: middle school, high school, college, and professional. The questions span 52 diverse disciplines... C-EVAL is accompanied by C-EVAL HARD, a subset of very challenging subjects

url.evidence: The C-EVAL data and evaluation code are available at https://github.com/hkust-nlp/ceval.
